content.comment_body: Hello, I am working on a project using Node-RED to communicate with two [product_name] devices. One is the latest model ([article_no]) and the other is an older version ([article_no]). The new version operates correctly—I can read and write to its memory. However, I can't reach the older one. Is there a communication difference between the models? The new version supports Modbus/TCP; could this be the reason they behave differently? Regards, [user_name]

Not all [product_name] devices with article number [article_no] support Modbus TCP/IP. This depends on the firmware. If the firmware is earlier than [version_no], Modbus TCP/IP isn't available. You can check firmware via the software: Extras > Transfer > Show firmware version. If your [product_name] runs [version_no], it cannot use Modbus TCP/IP.
Node-RED is now communicating with both [product_name] devices. Instead of Modbus, I am using the Ethernet S7 protocol as described at [url]. Thanks, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: The main topic is compatibility between different [product_name] versions when linking with third-party automation solutions. Users found that hardware and especially firmware versions impact supported communication protocols, such as Modbus TCP/IP. Initial confusion about connectivity was resolved by learning about product restrictions and using alternative protocols.
analysis.user_expectations: User anticipates efficient communication with both [product_name] models via Node-RED, expecting similar protocol support like Modbus TCP. The goal is to read and write memory on both devices through a unified interface.
